questions.question: In the early 1900s, which German climatologist divided the world's climate into different categories based on temperature, amount of rainfall and the time of year when rainfall occurs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wladimir Koppen.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Wladimir Köppen,** German meteorologist and climatologist best known for his **delineation and mapping of the climatic regions of the world**.
 
• The Köppen climate classification **divides climates into five main climate groups, with each group being divided based on seasonal precipitation and temperature patterns**. 
 
• The five main groups are** A (tropical), B (arid), C (temperate), D (continental), and E (polar). Each group and subgroup is represented by a letter.**
 
• The Köppen climate classification system **categorizes climate zones throughout the world based on local vegetation**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Michael Wille is an **American artist residing outside of Chicago in Normal, **IL. Wille is a Full Professor of Art at Illinois State University.​ 
 
• **Rudolf Oskar Robert Williams Geiger **was a **German meteorologist and climatologist. **
 
• **Alfred Lothar Wegener **was a German climatologist, geologist, geophysicist, meteorologist, and polar researcher.

questions.question: Which is the toxin-causing bacterium that spoils cream, cheese and milk and makes them taste bitter, sour or bitter?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Bacillus cereus.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The **bacterium Bacillus cereus** causes **spoilage of cream, cheese and milk** and makes them taste rancid, sour or bitter.
 
• **Bacillus cereus is a ****Gram-positive****, ****rod-shaped, facultatively anaerobic, motile, beta-hemolytic, spore-forming bacterium commonly found in soil, food and marine sponges**. 
 
• The specific name,** cereus, meaning "waxy" in Latin,** refers to the appearance of colonies grown on **blood agar.**
 
• Bacillus cereus is a foodborne pathogen that **can produce toxins, causing two types of gastrointestinal illness: the emetic (vomiting) syndrome and the diarrhoeal syndrome**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f2157f4370a0299e3616a8ad5a20656654003e95ee1bf26a58af24bec6c0ecc2.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Streptococcus thermophilus** also known as** Streptococcus salivarius subsp. thermophilus **is a gram-positive bacterium, and a fermentative facultative anaerobe, of the **viridans group.****​ **
 
• **Bifidobacterium **is a genus of gram-positive, nonmotile, often **branched anaerobic bacteria. **
 
• **Lactiplantibacillus plantarum** is a **widespread member of the genus Lactiplantibacillus** and commonly found in many fermented food products as well as** anaerobic plant matter.**

questions.question: What is a biotechnological process accomplished by yeast, some type of bacteria, or some other microorganism to convert sugar into ethyl alcohol and carbon dioxide?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alcoholic fermentation.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alcoholic fermentation** is a complex biochemical process during which **yeasts convert sugars to ethanol, carbon dioxide, and other metabolic byproducts that contribute to the chemical composition and sensorial properties of the fermented foodstuffs**.
 
• Alcoholic fermentation is the process of using yeast to convert sugars into alcohol.
 
• The main purpose of alcohol fermentation is **to produce ATP, the energy currency for cells, under anaerobic conditions**. 
 
• So from the yeast's perspective, carbon dioxide and ethanol are waste products.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9551d7d80f6f7ad4c1cd65f0e77aeea7d9215f1ca473ac115af87b50b5e4e5ee.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pasteurisation** is a process in which packaged and non-packaged foods are treated with mild heat, usually to** less than 100 °C, **to **eliminate pathogens and extend shelf life.** 
 
• **Lactic acid fermentation** is a metabolic process by which glucose or other six-carbon sugars are converted into **cellular energy and the metabolite lactate**, which is the lactic acid in solution.
 
• Glycolysis is **a cytoplasmic pathway that breaks down glucose into two three-carbon compounds and generates energy**.

questions.question: Which of the following name was used for the Indian subcontinent by ancient travellers like Megasthenes, FaHien, Huen Tsang, Al Beruni, Ibn Batuta etc. for the active contribution of Indian traders?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swaran Bhoomi.**____** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Swaran Bhoomi**

 
 
• **'Swaran Bhoomi'** was used for the Indian subcontinent by ancient travellers like** Megasthenes, FaHien, Huen Tsang, Al Beruni, Ibn Batuta etc.**
 
• Between the first to seventh centuries, India was the largest economy of the ancient and Medieval World.
 
• Approximately** one-third to one-fourth** **of the world's wealth** is under their control.
 
• In the writings of several travelers, the country was referred to as** Swaranbhumi and Swaran deep.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Suvarnabhumi **appears in many ancient Indian literary sources and Buddhist texts.
 
• Suvarnabhumi means **"Golden Land".**
 
• Ancient sources have associated it with one of a variety of places throughout the Southeast Asia region.
 
• There were texts mentioning Suvarnabhumi as a land of fortune where an Ancient Prince's ship was boarded for trade.
 
• Suvarnabhumi is known to be a land of richness and abundance.

questions.question: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek was known for which discovery in late 17th century?

options.text: Discovery of the properties of a stem cell
Discovery of the role of ATP as the source of energy for cells
Discovery of nucleus in the cell

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Observation of bacteria and protozoa. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Leeuwenhoek is universally acknowledged as the father of microbiology. 
 
• He discovered both protists and bacteria.
 
• More than being the first to see this unimagined world of 'animalcules', he was the first even to think of looking—certainly, the first with the power to see.
 
• Antonie van Leeuwenhoek used single-lens microscopes, which he made, to make the first observations of bacteria and protozoa. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The key properties of a stem cell were first defined by Ernest McCulloch and James Till at the University of Toronto and the Ontario Cancer Institute in the early 1960s.​ 
 
• The ATP molecule was discovered in the year 1929 by German chemist Karl Lohmann.
 
• Robert Brown discovered the nucleus of the cell in 1804.

questions.question: The ‘Room on the roof’ a novel about an orphaned English boy living with his guardian is written by whom among the following authors?

• The novel revolves around **Rusty**, an orphaned seventeen-year-old Anglo-Indian boy living in Dehradun.

questions.question: Which of the following Indian cities will host the International Olympic Committee session in 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Mumbai__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) won the bid to host the International Olympic Committee’s (IOC) next session in Mumbai in 2023.
 
• The IOC Session is the general meeting of the Members of the IOC and is held at least once every year.
 
• Important decisions regarding host cities for upcoming events, inclusion or exclusion of sports and federations and changes in the Olympic Charter are made at the IOC Sessions.
 
• Olympic gold medallist Abhinav Bindra, IOC member Nita Ambani, IOA president Narinder Batra and sports minister Anurag Thakur presented India’s proposal for the hosting rights at this year’s IOC Session, the 139th edition, in Beijing.
 
• Beijing is currently hosting the 2022 Winter Olympics.India won the bid after 75 members voted in favour of Mumbai while one voted against it.
 
• The IOC Session 2023, returning to the country after 40 years, will be held in May or June at the state-of-the-art Jio World Centre in Mumbai.
 
• India last hosted an IOC Session in 1983 in New Delhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• The International Olympic Committee is a non-governmental sports organisation based in Lausanne, Switzerland.
 
• The IOC is the governing body of the National Olympic Committees (NOCs) and of the worldwide "Olympic Movement", the IOC's term for all entities and individuals involved in the Olympic Games.
 
• As of 2020, there are 206 NOCs officially recognised by the IOC.
 
• The current president of the IOC is Thomas Bach.
 
• The Indian Olympic Association or Indian Olympic Committee is the body responsible for selecting athletes to represent India at the Olympic Games, Asian Games and other international athletic meets and for managing the Indian teams at these events.

questions.question: The historical fiction novel ‘The King Within’ is authored by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nandini Sengupta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"The King Within" **is** **authored by Nandini Sen Gupta, written in an extremely easy flowing language and vivid detailing, makes the characters come alive.
 
• **Nandini Sengupta** is a Pondicherry-based writer and journalist.
 
• After a chance trip to the Ajanta and Ellora caves in 2007, she began researching third and fourth-century **India** which quickly deepened into an obsession with India's glorious past.
 
• Her first book of fiction, The King Within, was published by **HarperCollins India** in 2017.
 
• Her first published work as an author was a non-fiction title called **Babies from the Heart **published by Random House India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Krishna Sobti **was an Indian Hindi-language fiction writer and essayist. She won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1980 for her novel Zindaginama and in 1996, was awarded the Sahitya Akademi Fellowship, the highest award of the Akademi.
 
• **Indu Sundaresan** is an Indian-American author of historical fiction. She is also the author of The Splendor of Silence, historical fiction set in a fictional Indian princely state just before Indian independence in 1947. Her work has been translated into some 23 languages worldwide.
 
• **Kiran Nagarkar** was an Indian novelist, playwright and screenwriter. A noted drama and film critic, he was one of the most significant writers of post-colonial India.

questions.question: Who among the following was appointed as the head coach of the Indian cricket team in November 2021?

The correct answer is __**Rahul Dravid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• Rahul Dravid will take over the new role and begin his tenure as India's full-time coach from the home **T20I series** against New Zealand starting November 17.
 
• Rahul Dravid replaced coach **Ravi Shastri**, whose stint comes to an end after the T20 World Cup.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Ravishankar Shastri** is the former head coach of the India national cricket team, a cricket commentator and former captain of Indian Cricket Team

questions.question: Identify the word that means vertical columns of Periodic Table.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Groups**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The vertical columns of Periodic Table is called **Groups**.
 
• In chemistry, a group is a **column** of elements in the periodic table of the chemical elements.
 
• There are **18** numbered groups in the periodic table; the f-block columns (between groups 2 and 3) are not numbered.
 
• The elements in a **group** have similar physical or chemical characteristics of the outermost electron shells of their atoms (i.e., the same core charge), because most chemical properties are dominated by the orbital location of the outermost electron.
 
• Groups may also be identified using their **topmost element**, or have a specific name.
 
• For example, group 16 is also described as the "**oxygen group**" and as the "**chalcogens**".
 
• An exception is the "**iron group**", which usually refers to "**group 8**", but in chemistry may also mean iron, cobalt, and nickel, or some other set of elements with similar chemical properties.
 
• In astrophysics and nuclear physics, it usually refers to iron, cobalt, nickel, chromium, and manganese.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In chemistry and physics, a **valence electron** is an electron in the outer shell associated with an atom, and that can participate in the formation of a chemical bond if the outer shell is not closed.
 
• A **period** in the periodic table is a row of chemical elements. All elements in a row have the same number of electron shells. 
 
• The k, l, m, and n are called atomic **orbitals**. Filling up these orbitals with electrons builds atoms, and the way in which atoms are built up gives rise to the periodic table.

questions.question: Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma was an exponent of which Indian classical dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma**, popularly known as Satyam, was an Indian classical dancer and choreographer, considered by many as one of the leading exponents of the classical dance form of **Kuchipudi**.
 
• He was known for his portrayal of **female** characters such as Usha, Satyabhama, Deva Devi, Mohini, Sasirekha, and Gollabhama .
 
• He was a recipient of several honors including **Kalidas Samman, Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, and Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship**.
 
• The Government of India awarded him the fourth highest civilian honor of the** Padma Shri**, in 1970, for his contributions to Dance.
 
• It is said that once even Prime Minister** Jawaharlal Nehru **sat coyly next to Vedantam in the audience recollecting the role that Vedantam had played as a female and the immediate reaction to consider him as the character itself and the basic etiquette that a female is required to show in public.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odissi**, also referred to as Orissa in old literature, is a major ancient Indian classical dance that origin in the Hindu temples of Odisha – an eastern coastal state of India.
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is a major form of Indian classical dance that originated in Tamil Nadu. The dance form is also briefly mentioned in Kannada text Manasollasa written by Someshwara III.
 
• **Kathak** is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance.It is the classical dance form of Uttar Pradesh. The origin of Kathak is traditionally attributed to the traveling bards in the of ancient northern India known as Kathakars or storytellers.

questions.question: A judge of the High Court retires at the age of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**62**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The judge of High court retires at the age of 62.**
 
• According to Article 124(2) of the Constitution, the age of retirement for Supreme Court judges is **65**.
 
• As per Article 217(1) of the Constitution, **High Court judges** retire at **62**.
 
• Initially, the retirement age of High Court judges was 60, which was later in 1963 increased to 62 through the **15th constitutional amendment Bill**.
 
• The idea of increasing the age of **retirement** for judges has been mooted for decades as a solution for dealing with mounting pendency of cases and judicial vacancies. It has also been discussed in the context of ensuring serving judges do not look for post-retirement jobs from the executive.
 
• Attorney General for India **K K Venugopal** has been one of the vocal advocates of increasing tenure of the judges, and has consistently spoken about it at every farewell of Supreme Court judges since 2017.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** High Courts** of India are the highest courts of appellate jurisdiction in each State and Union Territory of India.
 
• Judges in a high court are appointed by the **president of India** in consultation with the chief justice of India and the governor of the state under Art 217 of the Constitution but through subsequent judicial interpretations, the primacy of the appointment process is in the hands of the Judicial Collegium. High courts are headed by a chief justice.
 
• The chief justices rank **fourteenth** (within their respective states) and **seventeenth** (outside their respective states) on the Indian order of precedence.
 
• The number of judges in a court is decided by dividing the average institution of main cases during the last **five years** by the national average, or the average rate of disposal of main cases per judge per year in that high court, whichever is higher.

questions.question: The Regional Rural Banks Act was passed in __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1976**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Regional Rural Banks Act was passed in **1976**.
 
• Regional Rural Banks were established under the provisions of an ordinance passed on 26 September 1975 and **the RRB Act 1976 **to provide sufficient banking and credit facility for agriculture and other rural sectors.
 
• As a result, **five RRBs **were set up on 2 October 1975 on the recommendations of the Narasimham Committee on Rural Credit, during the tenure of Indira Gandhi's government.
 
• The purpose was to include rural areas into the economic mainstream since around** 70%** of the Indian population was rural.
 
• **Prathama Bank,** with head office in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh was the first RRB. It was sponsored by Syndicate Bank and had an authorised capital of Rs. 5 crore.
 
• The other **four** RRBs were Gaur Gramin Bank (sponsored by UCO Bank), Gorakhpur Kshetriya Gramin Bank (sponsored by State Bank of India), Haryana Kshetriya Gramin Bank (sponsored by Punjab National Bank), and Jaipur-Nagaur Anchalik Gramin Bank (sponsored by UCO Bank).
 
• The RRBs were owned by the central government, state government, and the sponsoring bank with **50%, 15%, and 35% **shareholding respectively

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Companies Act 1956 **was an Act of the Parliament of India, enacted in 1956, which enabled companies to be formed by registration, and set out the responsibilities of companies, their directors and secretaries.
 
• The** Consumer Protection Act,1986** was an Act by the Parliament of India enacted to protect the interests of consumers in India. It was replaced by the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 .
 
• The **Seed Act 1966 **was passed by the Indian Parliament on 29th December 1966 and it came into force from 2nd October, 1969. In addition, Seed Regulation Order was also passed in December 1983. The sole objective of this Act and Order has been to ensure that the Indian farmers get good quality seeds of important crops.

questions.question: Dr. Purushottam Dadheech, who was awarded the prestigious Padma Shri award in 2020, is associated with which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dr. Purushottam Dadheech is a **Kathak** dancer. He is a choreographer and educator of Indian classical dance and is known for his pioneering work in the field of Kathak.
 
• The oldest Kathak department which was formed in **1956** at Indira Kala Sangeet Vishwavidyalaya Public University located in Khairagarh, Purushottam Dadheech instated the **first Kathak syllabus** in 1961.
 
• He is the holder of the first Doctorate in Kathak Classical Dance and emphasizes the relevance of **Shastras** (Indian Ancient Dance treatises like Natyashastra and Nandikeshvara's Abhinaya Darpana) in the Kathak repertoire.
 
• He was awarded** Padma Shri**, the 4th highest civilian award in India.
 
• He is currently serving as the **Director** of the world’s first dedicated Kathak Research Centre at the Sri Sri University, Cuttack called Sri Sri Centre for Advanced Research in Kathak.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohiniyattam**, is an Indian classical dance form that developed and remained popular in the state of Kerala. 
 
• **Kuchipudi** is one of the eight major Indian classical dances. It originates from a village named Kuchipudi in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• **Odissi**, also referred to as Orissa in old literature, is a major ancient Indian classical dance that origin in the Hindu temples of Odisha – an eastern coastal state of India.
